newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGRI-LA SHARES HIT, FORECASTS CUT.
newsitem.headline: SHANGRI-LA SHARES HIT, FORECASTS CUT.

text.p: Shares of Shangri-La Asia Ltd took a hit on Thursday as some analysts looked to downgrade their full-year earnings estimates after it reported a decline in net profit for the first half.
The stock fell HK$0.40 to close at HK$8.40.
Shangri-La Asia posted a 6.3 percent fall in interim net profit on Wednesday to HK$470.95 million.
Cathy Anderson, an analyst with DBS Securities, said she had revised her estimate for 1997 to HK$1.08 billion from HK$1.16 billion. Shangri-La had net profit of HK$1.09 billion in 1996.

"My previous forecast for net interim profits was HK$510.4 million," said Anderson, adding that earnings in the first half had been slightly lower than expected mainly because tax was higher than anticipated.
Shangri-La Asia Ltd blamed its decline in net profit for the first six months of the year on start-up losses at its three new hotels in China and higher interest expenses and tax charges.
"A lot of people had assumed there would be a tax holiday for the three new hotels in China," said Anderson.

Philp Chan, an analyst with Yamaichi International, said he would also revise down his full-year estimate but had not yet finalised the figure. "We were expecting two to three percent growth in the first half," he said.
Chan said Shangri-La Asia's acquisition of hotel manager SLIM International Ltd was a good move for the company.
Shangri-La has agreed to buy 100 percent of SLIM International from its parent the Kuok Group for HK$1.2 billion to be paid through the issue of 135.9 million new shares at HK$8.83 each.
"From a business point of view it is a good move... as it provides a way for Shangri-La to capitalise management expertise," he said.

Chan said the planned spin-off of the China World Trade Centre Ltd, a Sino-foreign joint venture owned 50 percent by Shangri-La Asia, later this year, might boost the company's earnings in the second half. "If the spin-off goes ahead, Shangri-La may record exceptional gains," he said.

Second-half earnings might also be boosted by the inclusion of three months of SLIM International's profits, but that would be offset by added interest expenses and tax from the three loss-making hotels in China, and interest from a US$500 million loan signed recently, Anderson added.
